patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient was brought to the emergency department because of sudden, painless loss of vision in her right eye that occurred 30 minutes ago while watching TV. She has a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus but has had trouble adhering to her medication regimen.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with sudden loss of vision in one eye.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: I’m 60, and I came in because I suddenly lost vision in my right eye about 30 minutes ago while I was watching TV. It wasn’t painful, and I haven’t noticed any other symptoms. I also have trouble sticking to my medications for my heart, blood pressure, and diabetes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: No, I haven’t noticed any swelling in my joints. I’ve just had the sudden, painless loss of vision in my right eye.

turns.patient_answer: No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp.

turns.patient_answer: No, I haven’t had any itching or a persistent urge to scratch anywhere. It’s just been the sudden, painless loss of vision in my right eye that started about 30 minutes ago.

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble lifting your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes, I can lift my arms above my head without any trouble. I haven’t had any weakness or other symptoms—just the sudden, painless loss of vision in my right eye.”
